# Tool catalogue — every script, its flags and its phase

Opened from `SKILL.md` when a phase needs a tool's flags. Run from the skill folder (`npm install` once; playwright + jsdom).

**Output convention.** `design-contract.mjs`, `content-contract.mjs`, `verify-render.mjs`, `checkpoint.mjs`, `visual/group-verdict.mjs`, `visual/group-pages.mjs` and `visual/recheck.mjs` print ONE summary line, `<tool> <command>: <key=value …> -> <file>`, and write the complete JSON result to that file. `--out FILE` chooses the file; it is accepted in one form only — a path without `..` segments that is not a symbolic link, directory or hard-linked file — and is refused, before the command changes anything (exit 1, or 2 for `port-checks`, `group-pages`, `group-verdict`, `recheck`, `verify-render`, `checkpoint`) when it resolves to a file the command reads, a directory of its inputs (spec directory, run directory) or evidence it owns (`STATUS.md`, the controller's ledger, the audit receipt). A path in a printed line is percent-encoded when it holds a control character, `%` or (in `port-checks` rows) `|`; `decodeURIComponent` restores it; without it the file is `$TMPDIR/tracy-cli/<tool>-<command>-<hash of cwd and inputs>.json`, so keep evidence in the dossier with an explicit `--out`. `--json` prints the complete result to stdout instead (and also writes `--out` when given). `recheck.mjs --verbose` is `--json`; its answered requests point at the existing `<id>.result.json`; `group-pages.mjs --kind` writes the complete result of the kind to `<out-dir>/group-pages-<kind>.json` (beside the unchanged `route-plan.json`) and `--json` prints the same `{kind, pages, routes, pairs, plan, files}`. Exit codes are unchanged: the verdict is in the exit status, not in the printed form. A tool whose full output is wanted by a script uses `--json`; an agent reads the summary and opens the file only for the part it needs.

| `port-checks.mjs --run-root <dossier> [--verify <evidence>/verify.json] [--fast-gate <run>/FAST-GATE.json] [--group-verdict <verdict.json>] [--json] [--out rows.json]` | **Compact gate results — use it instead of opening check scripts.** Read-only: opens the reports the gates already wrote and prints one line per gate, `<id> \| PASS\|FAIL\|NOT-RUN \| <reason, one line> \| <detail file>`; the detail is the report itself, never printed. Gates: `port-audit` (`<run-root>/port-audit.json`, always), `verify.<fast\|full>.<parity\|scan\|shoot>` (`verify.mjs` output; the modes the run asked for; a report whose `ok` is still `null` is an unfinished run and its phases are NOT-RUN, never PASS), `fast-gate` (`FAST-GATE.json`), `group-verdict` (`verdict.json`); the last three only when their path is given — it never looks for "the newest" report. Status: **PASS** = the recorded success (`ok`, `status: pass`, `verdict: done`, with no recorded gap); **FAIL** = a recorded unsuccessful verdict, or a report that is unreadable or malformed; **NOT-RUN** = report missing, phase not reached (a red fast run leaves the full matrix NOT-RUN), or a group verdict `incomplete`. A patch-scope `port-audit` that passes still lists its bookkeeping advisories in the reason. Exit 0 only when every selected gate is PASS, 1 otherwise, 2 for a usage error. It reports **recorded** evidence: a PASS is the earlier gate's verdict, not a new live verification — re-run the gate when the port changed since. | 8, 8b, 9 |

| `visual/interaction-parity.mjs` (part of every `visual-qa.mjs` run → `interaction.json`, visual.json `interaction`) | What a person DOES, measured with a real pointer on the site and the source at the same widths: every drawer submenu the source can open (to 3 levels, 390 and 768, light and dark) must open on the site and show its children — `aria-expanded` alone is not an opening (`drawer-submenu-not-opened`/`-missing`/`-children-missing`), no overlap (a drill-down level drawn over its parents is a level change, not an overlap — it must show ONE back row and the back row must work: `drawer-back-inert`/`-duplicate`), same model, dark contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (one text failing in every state is one finding); tablet taps (1024/1180, controls ≥ 24×24 px, unobstructed); first click on the dark toggle; carousels reach every item; **header at 390/768/992/1024/1180/1280/1440**: height and control centres within 2 px, a button/link the source hides at a width but the site shows (`responsive-visibility`), a label on more lines than the source (`label-wrap`), the current section highlighted on article, event and donation pages and no second section lit (`nav-current-missing`/`-wrong`/`-extra`); the header logo is measured by what it paints, a wrapper's spacing is not header height; **pairing is by role, place and shape, not by name** (`lib/control-pairing.mjs`; rules in `visual-qa.md` §Interaction parity — a disclosure beside a link is no menu button, the current section is read per side, forms pair by purpose, findings are also grouped by cause in `groups`); **forms**: same required controls (controls pair by label, "Your name" = "Name"; controls that share a label pair in order when the label repeats as often on both sides with the same field types and none is a checkbox or radio, else the form is not measured; a source control the site lacks is `form-control-missing`; site-search forms are the header's search, not a form), an enabled submit once only the required ones are set, a disabled submit visibly distinct (`form-*`). Forms are filled, never sent (writes are aborted). Its findings are advisory (`notes/advisory.md`), never a verdict or an exit code (`visual-qa.md` §Interaction parity). A page the contract declares with an error status (the 404 page) is read only when it answers exactly that status, on both sides; any other answer to it, and an error answer to any other page, is no page (`notMeasured`). `measure-design.mjs` reads `<spec>/design-contract.json` and a plan shaped as `{"rules":[{"id":"body-type","category":"typography","selector":"body","pages":["home","about"],"properties":["font-family","font-size"]}]}`. Each rule must name distinct contract page IDs and CSS properties. It opens each planned page once per contract variant, applies the contract theme hook, waits for fonts and layout settling, then captures the requested selectors with `design-probe.mjs`. It checks the final URL after navigation and again against the probe URL, so a delayed client-side redirect is unmeasured. A page/variant is also unmeasured when navigation changes its origin or path, the requested theme does not apply, or its declared identity selector is absent. A rule property is measured only when every visible match on every planned page has a non-empty computed value and all values agree. Missing matches, missing values, mode failures, redirects, identity failures, and disagreements remain explicit `unmeasured` results with page/element evidence and differing values. New rules are added to the candidate only when all planned properties measured for all variants. An existing rule is updated only when all its contract pages are included in the plan and every planned property measured for every variant; its selector and category stay fixed. Candidate additions apply only to measured pages named by the plan. The command always writes both output files. `observations.json` records candidate validation: remaining pending notes or missing categories make it not yet valid (exit 0); any other validation error is reported as a failure (exit 1). Spec inputs remain untouched.

Two different wp-cli runners: build stand = `docker compose --progress quiet --project-directory <stand>
-p <project> run --rm -T cli`; clean stand = `docker run --rm --network <project>_default --user 33:33
-v <stand>/verify:/var/www/html -e WORDPRESS_DB_* … wordpress:cli wp`. `lib/wp-cli.mjs` turns both forms
into **one kept-alive container** (`<project>-cli-keep`, cleaned up when the process exits) and `docker exec`s
each command — 0.3–0.5 s instead of 2–3 s per command (measured 14/09); `--wp-keep off` / `TRACY_WP_KEEP=0` to turn it off. Gotcha 18
still holds when it is off. `unset DOCKER_HOST` first.

**Source routes without URL rewrite.** A Joomla source with no SEF rewrite answers `/index.php/<path>` (`/contact` → 404). Every live step that maps a site route to a source route resolves it through `scripts/lib/source-routes.mjs` — one route at a time (a source may answer one page directly and another under `/index.php`): the route as given, the same route under `/index.php`, and the real hrefs of the source's own home page. `motion`, `layout-boxes`, `preflight` (when `--source-prefix` is not given), Visual QA (`sourceRoute`), `port-audit` and `audit-live` all use it. A reachable pair whose routes cannot be resolved is a failure of the tool, never an environment note. Every route must answer 200, except a route the page map declares as not-found (a 404 page pair): it resolves to its declared status (`expect`, passed by Visual QA from each page's declared `status`) on the source as on the port, and any other status for it is unresolved.
